coordinates.locator: mean of the three hall positions geometry:daya-bay-eh1-hall, geometry:daya-bay-eh2-hall and geometry:daya-bay-eh3-hall (arXiv:1508.03943 Table 2 baselines; OSM reactor buildings)
coordinates.note: No source consulted gives surveyed coordinates for the Daya Bay near hall, Ling Ao near hall or far hall. This point is the mean of the three hall positions derived in the geometry records from the surveyed detector-to-core baselines of the Daya Bay detector-system paper and the OpenStreetMap reactor-building positions; each hall lies within about 0.85 km of it (the halls are up to 1.6 km apart), so it is shown as a campus-grade, approximate point and not as three hall-level points.

name: Daya Bay underground experimental halls
notes: Represents all three Daya Bay experimental halls (Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near, far) as one site record pending hall-specific sourced coordinates; see detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors placements for the three distinct roles (near/near/far) recorded against this shared point.
No overburden or depth figure for any hall was found in the sources consulted (checked 2026-09-17).

summary.plain: The underground halls near Shenzhen, China, where Daya Bay's detectors sat close to nuclear reactors to catch antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Underground experimental complex comprising the Daya Bay near hall, Ling Ao near hall and far hall, at baselines of 470 m, 576 m and 1648 m respectively from six 2.9 GW_th reactor cores at the Daya Bay/Ling Ao nuclear power complex, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China.
